question.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨0,12,-6⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}12y-6z-30 & =0 \\ -6z & =-12y+30 \\ z & =2y-5\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $y=0$, we get $z=-5.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-5)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-5⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-5⟩)\cdot ⟨0,12,-6⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
